name: BEVAN, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Idaho parental choice tax credit is constitutional as Article IX, section 1 sets a floor, not a ceiling, for legislative power regarding education, and the tax credit serves a public purpose.

name: MOELLER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the decision clarifies the meaning of the constitutional provisions without altering the fundamental constitutional foundation for public education in Idaho.

name: BEVAN, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that drug dog sniffs are not searches under the Idaho Constitution and that the automobile exception does not require a heightened standard.

name: ZAHN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the FIS and short ballot title failed to substantially comply with Idaho law, requiring revisions, but the long ballot title did comply.

name: BRODY, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Twin Falls City waste collection ordinance did not create an objectively reasonable expectation of privacy in curbside garbage, and therefore, the warrantless searches did not violate the Idaho Constitution.

name: ZAHN, Justice
description: Concurred in the result, but dissented from the majority's analysis regarding the applicability of the Idaho Parental Rights Act and the standard of review, arguing that strict scrutiny should apply to the guardianship statutes.

name: ZAHN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that while Article V, section 13 of the Idaho Constitution does not empower the legislature to mandate consecutive sentences, the power to do so was not exclusively reserved to the judiciary at common law, thus Idaho Code section 19-2520G(3) does not violate the separation of powers.

name: BRODY, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that House Bills 124 and 340 are reasonable exercises of the legislature's authority to enact conditions on the right of suffrage and pass rational basis review.

name: BEVAN, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that while Idaho Code section 6-311A is constitutional for purely equitable claims, a jury trial is required for legal claims or issues of fact presented by the pleadings in unlawful detainer cases.

name: ZAHN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Idaho Code section 67-5224(5)(c) is constitutional because rulemaking authority is a legislative delegation, not a constitutional power of the executive branch, and Article III, section 29 permits legislative review of all administrative rules, including pending ones.

name: STEGNER
description: Concurred, argued that the district court correctly found that Idaho Code section 67-3004(10) impinges on the Supreme Court's prerogative to make its own rules governing its own procedure.

name: ZAHN, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that the district court correctly denied the motion to suppress and that neither the Idaho nor the United States Constitution guarantees a specific number of peremptory challenges.

name: BEVAN, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the plaintiffs failed to demonstrate a particularized injury or a traceable causal connection between the proposed development and their alleged harms, thus lacking standing under Idaho's adopted federal standing principles.

name: STEGNER, J.
description: Dissented, argued that Idaho's standing requirements should be broader than federal standards, as the Idaho Constitution grants wider access to courts, and Tidwell should have standing to challenge governmental conduct.

name: JUSTICE TROUT, pro tem
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's interpretation of standing unnecessarily restrains Idahoans from having their claims resolved by Idaho courts.

name: Bevan
description: Concurred, argued that the Idaho Constitution prohibits warrantless arrests for completed misdemeanors unless the offense occurred in the arresting officer's personal presence, and collective knowledge cannot bypass this requirement.

name: Moeller
description: Dissented, argued that the collective knowledge doctrine should apply to misdemeanor arrests and that the majority's ruling unnecessarily hinders law enforcement's ability to protect the public.

name: MOELLER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the district court's judgment was affirmed in part and reversed in part, specifically reversing the ITCA bar on individual refunds for unconstitutional street impact fees but affirming other rulings.

name: STEGNER, JUSTICE.
description: Concurred, argued that the federal 4-R Act does not preempt Idaho's constitutional requirement for uniform property taxation, and that genuine issues of material fact exist regarding the equalization of operating property compared to other commercial property.

name: ZAHN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Pool's waiver of Fourth Amendment rights constituted consent to warrantless searches of her residence, and since Idaho's Article I, section 17 rights were coextensive in this instance, the search was lawful.

name: BRODY
description: Concurred, argued that the Idaho Constitution does not implicitly guarantee a fundamental right to abortion, as such a right is not "deeply rooted" in Idaho's history and traditions, and the challenged laws are rationally related to legitimate governmental purposes.

name: ZAHN, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Idaho Constitution's Inalienable Rights Clause implicitly protects a pregnant woman's fundamental right to obtain an abortion to preserve her life or health, based on the plain language, history, and traditions.

name: STEGNER, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Idaho Constitution provides broader fundamental rights to women, including a fundamental right to obtain an abortion to protect their life, liberty, and safety, and that the majority's decision strips women of these basic rights.

name: MOELLER, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the failure to comply with statutory arrest notice requirements does not constitute a constitutional violation that would warrant the suppression of evidence.

name: STEGNER, J.
description: Dissented, argued that a violation of Idaho Code section 19-608 constitutes an unlawful arrest and an unreasonable seizure under the Idaho Constitution, requiring suppression of evidence.

name: MOELLER, Justice
description: Concurred with the majority opinion, finding Idaho Code section 20-1016 constitutional as the 1986 amendment allows the legislature to define the commutation process, including gubernatorial review for serious cases.

name: HORTON, J. pro tem
description: Concurred in the result, but dissented from the majority's reasoning that Idaho Code section 20-1016(2) is constitutional, arguing it impermissibly transfers commutation power from the Commission to the Governor. However, he concurred in the outcome due to the lack of an effective statute for the Commission to commute the sentence.

name: MOELLER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the district court erred in finding the conversation length immeasurable and that the deviations did not unlawfully prolong the traffic stop because the drug dog alerted before the traffic stop's mission was completed.

name: STEGNER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while the result is correct under federal Fourth Amendment jurisprudence, Idaho's constitution should provide greater protection against dog sniff searches, requiring at least reasonable suspicion.

name: STEGNER, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that victims do not have standing in a criminal case to independently seek renewal of a judgment for an order of restitution, as criminal proceedings are between the State and the defendant.

name: STEGNER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Commission timely filed its report and acted within its power regarding precinct splitting, as the ninety-day deadline began when the Commission elected its co-chairs, and the statutory escape clause applied to both legislative and congressional plans.

name: STEGNER, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the petitioners failed to prove that Plan L03 was unconstitutional under federal or state law, and that the Commission reasonably balanced competing interests in creating the plan.

name: BRODY, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Randall's Fourth Amendment rights were violated when the drug dog leapt inside his car without a warrant or consent, as this constituted an unconstitutional search for information.

name: STEGNER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the U.S. Supreme Court's Fourth Amendment jurisprudence is flawed by not classifying an exterior dog sniff as a search, and that the Idaho Constitution provides greater privacy protections, making any drug dog sniff a search.

name: BEVAN, Chief Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the drug dog's instinctive entry into the vehicle did not constitute police misconduct and therefore did not violate the Fourth Amendment, and that applying the exclusionary rule in such cases does not serve its purpose of deterring police.

name: STEGNER, J.
description: Concurred with the ultimate holding but argued that the federal standing framework is legally unsound and constitutionally incorrect for Idaho courts.

name: BRODY, J.
description: Concurred that SB 1110 is unconstitutional but dissented from applying strict scrutiny, arguing the "reasonable and workable" standard should have been used.

name: BEVAN, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that the warrantless arrest for a completed misdemeanor DUI was unlawful because the officer lacked sufficient personal knowledge at the time of arrest to establish probable cause for a felony, violating Amstutz's constitutional rights.

name: BRODY, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that Sutterfield's arrest was a valid citizen's arrest, and the failure to fully comply with statutory notice requirements did not rise to the level of a constitutional violation, thus suppression of evidence was not the appropriate remedy.

name: STEGNER, J.
description: Dissented, arguing that Sutterfield was unlawfully arrested when handcuffed prior to any citizen's arrest, and that the majority's distinction between constitutional and statutory violations erodes protections against unreasonable searches and seizures.

name: BRODY, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Rule 41(f) does not require the return of contraband and that the prohibition of marijuana does not unconstitutionally infringe on religious liberty.

name: MOELLER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Idaho Code section 49-1405(1)(b) violates the Idaho Constitution by allowing warrantless arrests for misdemeanors committed outside an officer's presence, and evidence obtained from such an unlawful arrest cannot be used in administrative license suspension proceedings.

name: BRODY, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Idaho Code section 5-230 is constitutional, does not violate due process or equal protection rights, and equitable estoppel does not apply as SLRMC's statement was not a false representation of a past or existing fact.
